newsitem.title: USA: Ex-vice presidential hopeful Kemp seeks prosecutor.
newsitem.headline: Ex-vice presidential hopeful Kemp seeks prosecutor.

text.p: Unsuccessful Republican vice presidential candidate Jack Kemp added his voice Monday to the chorus calling for an independent counsel to investigate campaign fund-raising abuses.

Kemp, who ran with Republican presidential candidate Bob Dole last autumn, said so-called "soft money" -- unlimited donations from people and companies to political parties -- should be banned from politics.
"Clearly it's wrong and there should be no soft money in politics," Kemp said in a CNN interview.
"In my opinion, only an indpendent counsel and the Thompson committee can fully explore the -- I'm going to use the word -- corruption of political fund raising in America," he said.
A Senate committee headed by Republican Fred Thompson of Tennesse and a House committee are investigating campaign abuses centering on improper funds given Democrats.
Attorney General Janet Reno has rejected requests to set in motion the procedure for a special prosecutor, or independent counsel.
Instead she has named a task force of 25 FBI agents and prosecutors to investigate the growing uproar over campaign financing.
Kemp said investigators should inquire into activities of both presidential and congressional candidates.
Both Democrats and Republicans raised record amounts of money for the 1996 presidential election and congressional campaigns where nearly $2.7 billion was spent in the most expensive campaigns ever.
